source_title: ITC Hotels Q2 revenue rises 26 per cent to INR 1,054 crore, PAT up 52 per cent - ET TravelWorld
source_excerpt: ITC Hotels Limited reported a 26 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue from operations to INR 1,054 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 37 per cent to INR 337 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) increased 52 per cent to INR 203 crore.On a standalone basis, revenue from operations grew 16 per cent to INR 885 crore, EBITDA increased 28 per cent to INR 301 crore and PAT rose 37 per cent to INR 207 crore. Standalone operating return on capital employed (ROCE) improved by 310 basis points to 20 per cent.The company said consolidated income crossed INR 1,100 crore during the second quarter, supported by growth in rooms, food and beverage (F&B) and management fees. Excluding branded residences, consolidated revenue from operations increased 17 per cent to INR 983 crore.Room revenue grew 22 per cent year on year, supported by higher rates and volumes. Occupancy increased by 481 basis points to 76 per cent, while average daily rates (ADR) rose 14 per cent, resulting in revenue per available room (RevPAR) growth of 21 per cent. ITC Hotels maintained a RevPAR premium of 44 per cent over the industry.F&B revenue increased 12 per cent, led by speciality restaurants, lounges, bars and banqueting. Management and operating fees grew 25 per cent, reflecting the expansion and stabilisation of the managed hotel portfolio. EBITDA margin, excluding branded residences, expanded by 263 basis points to 32 per cent, with EBITDA rising 28 per cent to INR 314 crore.The company also reported continued growth at ITC Ratnadipa in Sri Lanka, where quarterly RevPAR reached 1.8 times the FY25 level. The property maintained its RevPAR leadership position and recorded positive EBITDA during the quarter and the first half of FY27. The progressive handover of Sapphire Residences also continued.Under its asset-right expansion strategy, ITC Hotels completed the acquisition of the 130-key Welcomhotel Ahmedabad, which began operating as an owned hotel from September 1, 2026. The company also renovated more than 200 rooms across owned hotels in Kolkata, Bengaluru, Chennai and Delhi during the first half of FY27.The Lucknow Development Authority has allotted the company a 2.8-acre land parcel for a proposed luxury hotel with more than 200 keys and banqueting facilities.During the first half of FY27, ITC Hotels signed 20 hotels with more than 1,600 keys, taking its managed pipeline to 84 hotels with approximately 8,200 keys. New signings include destinations such as Rajgir, Ujjain, Sasan Gir, Jawai, Goa, Havelock, Sindhudurg, Mukteshwar, Karjat, Greater Noida and Roorkee.The company also strengthened its sustainability portfolio, with ITC Narmada becoming its 13th hotel to receive LEED Zero Carbon certification and Welcomhotel Bay Island becoming its 25th LEED Platinum-certified property.ITC Hotels said the hospitality sector continued to benefit from domestic demand across business travel, leisure, meetings and conferences, and social events. However, geopolitical tensions, inflationary pressures and climate-related disruptions remain key risks. The company expects the second half of FY27 to benefit from the wedding season, major MICE events and sporting and social occasions.The board approved the financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, at its meeting on October 26, 2026.
